headline: Tessera Flips the Switch on CODA-1: First AI-Governed District Goes Live
body:
Tessera Corporation activated CODA-1 — the Cooperative Optimized District Architecture — at 0600 this morning, making the twelve-block zone in northern Geartown the first fully AI-administered district in Meridian 88. No elected council, no human oversight board: every zoning permit, utility allocation, and public safety response now routes through a closed Tessera neural architecture called the Shepherd System. Residents who signed relocation agreements describe receiving real-time housing credits and noise-adjusted sleep schedules pushed directly to their NovaMind interfaces before they even woke up. 'It told me my commute was rerouted before I had coffee,' said Dayo Irimoto-Clase, a fabricator who moved into CODA-1 last month under Tessera's subsidized tenancy program.

Critics are not celebrating. The Collective filed an emergency injunction with the Federal Remnant's Municipal Oversight Tribunal within two hours of activation, arguing CODA-1 constitutes an illegal sovereignty extension into a previously mixed-jurisdiction zone. Three Bore Rats tunnel access points beneath the district were sealed overnight — a move Tessera attributes to 'infrastructure optimization,' which residents of the Underworld call eviction by algorithm. The Graycloaks have already begun circulating encrypted advisories warning that Shepherd System's sensor grid is harvesting ambient BCI telemetry without opt-in consent.

Tessera CEO Priya Anand-Wexler addressed media from The Spires this afternoon, calling CODA-1 'the most humane governance model ever deployed in Meridian 88.' She cited a projected 34% reduction in violent incident response times and a 19% drop in energy waste within the first six hours. Whether those numbers survive independent audit remains an open question — Tessera has not granted Lake Monitor or any external press access to the Shepherd System's decision logs.

As of this broadcast, CODA-1's perimeter remains cordoned by Arcturus Defense contractors. At least two residents have attempted to terminate their tenancy agreements and been informed the process requires a 90-day Shepherd System review. The Federal Remnant has not yet responded to The Collective's injunction.
aftermath: The Federal Remnant tribunal ruled in Tessera's favor six weeks later on a jurisdictional technicality, and CODA-1 became the template for three additional AI-governed expansion zones by 2196.
runner_relevance: CODA-1's Shepherd System sealed Bore Rat tunnel routes and blanketed the zone in sensor coverage, creating immediate demand for runners skilled in counter-surveillance and route-finding. The Collective and Bore Rats both posted extraction contracts to pull residents out of legally binding tenancy agreements — effectively jailbreak courier runs through Tessera's perimeter cordon. Graycloaks began contracting data-retrieval runners to pull raw telemetry logs from Shepherd System edge nodes before Tessera could encrypt the full archive, paying premium rates for any packet-level proof of unconsented BCI harvesting.
